readings.title: Yiphtaḥ's Rash Vow
readings.subtitle: The tragic sacrifice of his only daughter.
readings.text: [Judges 11:29] And the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came upon Yiphtaḥ, and he passed through <dn>את</dn> Gil‛aḏ and <dn>את</dn> Menashsheh, and passed through <dn>את</dn> Mitspeh of Gil‛aḏ. And from Mitspeh of Gil‛aḏ he passed on toward the children of Ammon. [30] And Yiphtaḥ made a vow to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and said, “If <dn>You</dn> give <dn>את</dn> the children of Ammon into <dn>my</dn> hands, [31] then it shall be that whatever comes out of the doors of my house to meet me, when <dn>I</dn> return in peace from the children of Ammon, shall belong to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>I</dn> shall offer it up as an ascending offering.” [32] Yiphtaḥ then passed on toward the children of Ammon to fight against them, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave <dn>את</dn> them into his hands. [33] And he struck <dn>את</dn> them from Aro‛ěr as far as Minnith, twenty cities, and to Aḇěl Keramim, with a very great slaughter. Thus the children of Ammon were humbled before the children of Yisra’ěl. [34] And Yiphtaḥ came to his house at Mitspah, and saw <dn>את</dn> his daughter coming out to meet him with timbrels and dancing. Now except for her he had neither son nor daughter. [35] And it came to be, when he saw her, that he tore his garments, and said, “Oh my daughter! You have brought me very low, and you are among those who trouble me! And <dn>I</dn>, <dn>I</dn> have given <dn>my</dn> word to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>I</dn> am unable to turn back.” [36] And she said to him, “<dn>My</dn> father, if you have given your word to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, do to me according to what has gone out of your mouth, because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has taken <dn>את</dn> vengeance for you upon your enemies, <dn>את</dn> the children of Ammon.” [37] And she said to her father, “Let this be done for me: let me alone for two new moons, and let me go and wander on the mountains and bewail my maidenhood, my friends and <dn>I</dn>.” [38] Then he said, “Go.” And he sent her away for two new moons. And she went with her friends, and bewailed her maidenhood on the mountains. [39] And it came to be at the end of two new moons that she returned to her father, and he did to her as he had vowed, and she knew no man. And it became a statute in Yisra’ěl [40] that the daughters of Yisra’ěl went every year for four days to lament <dn>את</dn> the daughter of Yiphtaḥ the Gil‛aḏite.

readings.title: The Shibboleth Incident
readings.subtitle: Yiphtaḥ's conflict with the tribe of Ephrayim.
readings.text: [Judges 12:1] And the men of Ephrayim gathered together, and passed over toward Tsaphon, and said to Yiphtaḥ, “Why did you pass over to fight against the children of Ammon, and did not call us to go with you? We are going to burn <dn>את</dn> your house over you with fire!” [2] And Yiphtaḥ said to them, “<dn>My</dn> people and <dn>I</dn> were in a great struggle with the children of Ammon. And when <dn>I</dn> called you, you did not save me out of their hands. [3] “And <dn>I</dn> saw that you would not save me, then <dn>I</dn> took <dn>את</dn> my life in my hands and went over against the children of Ammon. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave <dn>את</dn> them into my hand. And why have you come up to me today to fight against me?” [4] Yiphtaḥ then gathered together <dn>את</dn> all the men of Gil‛aḏ and fought against Ephrayim. And the men of Gil‛aḏ struck <dn>את</dn> Ephrayim, because they had said, “You Gil‛aḏites are fugitives of Ephrayim in the midst of Ephrayim, in the midst of Menashsheh.” [5] And Gil‛aḏ captured <dn>את</dn> the fords of the Yarděn that faced Ephrayim. And it came to be, when the fugitives from Ephrayim said, “Let me pass over,” the men of Gil‛aḏ said to him, “You are an Ephrayimite!” If he said, “No,” [6] then they would say to him, “Please say, ‘Shibboleth’!” And he would say, “Sibboleth,” for he was unable to pronounce it right. Then they seized him and slew <dn>את</dn> him at the fords of the Yarděn. And at that time there fell forty-two thousand Ephrayimites. [7] And Yiphtaḥ ruled Yisra’ěl six years. And Yiphtaḥ the Gil‛aḏite died and was buried in one of the cities of Gil‛aḏ.

readings.title: Iḇtsan of Běyth Leḥem
readings.subtitle: A judge with thirty sons and thirty daughters.
readings.text: [Judges 12:8] And after him, Iḇtsan of Běyth Leḥem ruled Yisra’ěl. [9] And he came to have thirty sons and thirty daughters – he sent <dn>את</dn> abroad and brought in thirty daughters for his sons. And he ruled Yisra’ěl seven years. [10] And Iḇtsan died and was buried at Běyth Leḥem.

readings.title: Ělon the Zeḇulunite
readings.subtitle: He judged Yisra’ěl for ten years.
readings.text: [Judges 12:11] And after him Ělon the Zeḇulunite ruled Yisra’ěl. And he ruled Yisra’ěl ten years. [12] And Ělon the Zeḇulunite died and was buried at Ayalon in the land of Zeḇulun.

readings.title: Aḇdon the Pirathonite
readings.subtitle: A judge with forty sons and thirty grandsons.
readings.text: [Judges 12:13] And after him, Aḇdon son of Hillěl the Pirathonite ruled Yisra’ěl, [14] and he had forty sons and thirty grandsons, who rode on seventy young donkeys. And he ruled Yisra’ěl eight years. [15] And Aḇdon son of Hillěl the Pirathonite died and was buried in Pirathon in the land of Ephrayim, in the mountains of the Amalěqites.

readings.subsection: The Birth and Rise of Shimshon
readings.title: The Annunciation to Manovaḥ's Wife
readings.subtitle: A Messenger of YeHoVaH foretells the birth of a Nazirite.
readings.text: [Judges 13:1] And again the children of Yisra’ěl did <dn>את</dn> evil in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, so <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave <dn>את</dn> them into the hand of the Philistines for forty years. [2] And there was a certain man from Tsor‛ah, of the clan of the Danites, whose name was Manovaḥ. And his wife was barren and had not borne. [3] And a Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared to the woman and said to her, <dq>“See now, you are barren and have not borne, but you shall conceive, and you shall bear a son.</dq> [4] <dq>“And now, please guard, and do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat any unclean food.</dq> [5] <dq>“For look, you are conceiving and bearing a son. And let no razor come upon his head, for the youth is a Nazirite to <dn>Elohim</dn> from the womb on. And he shall begin to save <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl out of the hand of the Philistines.”</dq> [6] And the woman came and spoke to her husband, saying, “A Man of <dn>Elohim</dn> came to me, and <dn>His</dn> appearance was like the appearance of a Messenger of <dn>Elohim</dn>, very awesome. But <dn>I</dn> did not ask <dn>Him</dn> where <dn>He</dn> was from, and <dn>He</dn> did not declare to me <dn>His</dn> name. [7] “And <dn>He</dn> said to me, ‘See, you are conceiving and bearing a son. And now, drink no wine or strong drink, nor eat any unclean food, for the youth is a Nazirite to <dn>Elohim</dn> from the womb to the day of his death.’ ”

readings.subsection: The Birth and Rise of Shimshon
readings.title: The Wondrous Messenger
readings.subtitle: Manovaḥ and his wife offer a sacrifice and witness a miracle.
readings.text: [Judges 13:8] And Manovaḥ prayed to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and said, “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, please let <dn>את</dn> the Man of <dn>Elohim</dn> whom <dn>You</dn> sent come to us again and teach us what to do for the youth who is to be born.” [9] And <dn>Elohim</dn> listened to <dn>את</dn> the voice of Manovaḥ, and the Messenger of <dn>Elohim</dn> came to the woman again as she was sitting in the field, but Manovaḥ her husband was not with her. [10] And the woman ran hurriedly and informed her husband, and said to him, “See, <dn>He</dn> has appeared to me, the Man who came to me the other day!” [11] And Manovaḥ arose and went after his wife, and came to the Man, and he said to <dn>Him</dn>, “Are <dn>You</dn> the Man who spoke to this woman?” And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am.”</dq> [12] And Manovaḥ said, “Now let <dn>Your</dn> words come true! What is to be the rule for the youth’s life and his work?” [13] And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Manovaḥ, <dq>“Let the woman guard all that <dn>I</dn> said to her.</dq> [14] <dq>“Let her not eat any food that comes from the vine, neither let her drink wine or strong drink, or eat any unclean food. Let her guard all that which <dn>I</dn> have commanded her.”</dq> [15] And Manovaḥ said to the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “Please let us detain <dn>You</dn>, and prepare a young goat for <dn>You</dn>.” [16] And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Manovaḥ, <dq>“Though you detain <dn>Me</dn>, <dn>I</dn> do not eat your food. But if you offer an ascending offering, offer it to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”</dq> For Manovaḥ did not know <dn>He</dn> was a Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [17] Then Manovaḥ said to the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, “What is <dn>Your</dn> name? When <dn>Your</dn> words come true, then we shall esteem <dn>You</dn>.” [18] And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>“Why do you ask <dn>My</dn> name, since it is wondrous?”</dq> [19] And Manovaḥ took <dn>את</dn> the young goat with <dn>את</dn> the grain offering, and offered it upon the rock to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And <dn>He</dn> did wondrously while Manovaḥ and his wife looked on. [20] And it came to be, as the flame went up toward the heavens from the slaughter-place, that the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> went up in the flame of the slaughter-place. And Manovaḥ and his wife were watching, and they fell on their faces to the ground. [21] And the Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> did not appear any more to Manovaḥ and his wife. Then Manovaḥ knew that <dn>He</dn> was a Messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [22] And Manovaḥ said to his wife, “We shall certainly die, because we have seen <dn>Elohim</dn>!” [23] But his wife said to him, “If <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had been pleased to put us to death, <dn>He</dn> would not have accepted an ascending offering and a grain offering from our hands, nor would <dn>He</dn> have shown us all this, nor would <dn>He</dn> have let us hear the like of this!” [24] So the woman bore a son and called his name Shimshon. And the child grew, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> blessed <dn>את</dn> him. [25] And the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> began to move <dn>את</dn> him at Maḥaněh Dan, between Tsor‛ah and Eshta’ol.

readings.subsection: The Birth and Rise of Shimshon
readings.title: Shimshon's Philistine Wife
readings.subtitle: He kills a lion with his bare hands and later finds honey in its carcass.
readings.text: [Judges 14:1] And Shimshon went down to Timnah, and saw <dn>את</dn> a woman in Timnah of the daughters of the Philistines. [2] And he went up and informed his father and mother, saying, “<dn>I</dn> have seen a woman in Timnah of the daughters of the Philistines. And now, take <dn>את</dn> her for me for a wife.” [3] But his father and mother said to him, “Is there no woman among the daughters of your brothers, or among all <dn>my</dn> people, that you should take <dn>את</dn> a wife from the uncircumcised Philistines?” And Shimshon said to his father, “Take <dn>את</dn> her for me, for she is pleasing in <dn>my</dn> eyes.” [4] However, his father and mother did not know that it was of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that <dn>He</dn> was seeking an occasion to move against the Philistines. For at that time the Philistines were ruling over Yisra’ěl. [5] Then Shimshon went down to Timnah with his father and mother, and came to the vineyards of Timnah, and saw a young lion roaring as it met him. [6] And the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came mightily upon him, and he tore <dn>את</dn> it apart as the tearing apart of a young goat, with naught in his hand. But he did not make known to his father or his mother what he had done. [7] And he went down and spoke to the woman, and she pleased Shimshon well. [8] And when he returned later to take her, he turned aside to look at <dn>את</dn> the carcass of the lion, and saw a swarm of bees and honey in the carcass of the lion. [9] And he took some of it in his hands and went along, eating. And he came to his father and mother, and gave them, and they ate. But he did not make known to them that he took <dn>את</dn> the honey out of the carcass of the lion.

readings.subsection: The Birth and Rise of Shimshon
readings.title: The Riddle and the Betrayal
readings.subtitle: Shimshon's wife coaxes the answer from him, leading to his violent retribution.
readings.text: [Judges 14:10] So his father went down to the woman. And Shimshon gave a feast there, for young men used to do so. [11] And it came to be, when they saw him, that they brought thirty companions to be with him. [12] And Shimshon said to them, “Please let me put forth a riddle to you. If you clearly solve and explain it to me within the seven days of the feast, then <dn>I</dn> shall give you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of garments. [13] “But if you are unable to explain it to me, then you shall give me thirty linen shirts and thirty changes of garments.” And they said to him, “Put forth your riddle and let us hear it.” [14] And he said to them, “Out of the eater came forth food, and out of the strong came forth sweetness.” And for three days they were unable to explain <dn>את</dn> the riddle. [15] And it came to be on the seventh day that they said to Shimshon’s wife, “Entice your husband to explain <dn>את</dn> the riddle to us, or else we burn <dn>את</dn> you and <dn>את</dn> your father’s house with fire. Have you invited us in order to take what is ours? Is it not?” [16] And Shimshon’s wife wept before him, and said, “You only hate me, and do not love me! You have put forth a riddle to the sons of <dn>my</dn> people, but you have not explained it to me.” And he said to her, “Look, <dn>I</dn> have not explained it to <dn>my</dn> father or <dn>my</dn> mother, and should <dn>I</dn> explain it to you?” [17] And she had wept before him the seven days while their feast lasted. And it came to be on the seventh day that he informed her, because she pressed him so much. She then explained <dn>את</dn> the riddle to the sons of her people. [18] And the men of the city said to him on the seventh day before the sun went down, “What is sweeter than honey? And what is stronger than a lion?” And he said to them, “If you had not ploughed with <dn>my</dn> heifer, you would not have solved <dn>את</dn> my riddle!” [19] Then the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came upon him mightily, and he went down to Ashqelon and struck thirty of their men, stripped them, and gave <dn>את</dn> the changes of garments to those who had explained the riddle. And his displeasure burned, and he went back up to his father’s house. [20] And Shimshon’s wife was given to his companion, who had been his friend.

readings.subsection: The Birth and Rise of Shimshon
readings.title: Vengeance with Fire
readings.subtitle: Shimshon ties torches to the tails of three hundred foxes to burn Philistine fields.
readings.text: [Judges 15:1] And it came to be, after some time, in the days of wheat harvest, that Shimshon visited <dn>את</dn> his wife with a young goat. And he said, “Let me go in to <dn>my</dn> wife, into her room.” But her father would not permit him to go in. [2] And her father said, “Indeed, <dn>I</dn> thought that you hated her intensely; so <dn>I</dn> gave her to your companion. Is not her younger sister better than she? Please, take <dn>את</dn> her instead.” [3] And Shimshon said to them, “This time <dn>I</dn> am blameless regarding the Philistines if <dn>I</dn> do evil to them!” [4] And Shimshon went and caught three hundred foxes, and took <dn>את</dn> torches, and turned them tail to tail, and put a torch between each pair of tails, [5] and set the torches on fire, and sent <dn>את</dn> them out into the standing grain of the Philistines, and burned up <dn>את</dn> both the shocks and <dn>את</dn> the standing grain, even <dn>את</dn> the vineyards and <dn>את</dn> olive-trees. [6] And the Philistines said, “Who did this?” And they answered, “Shimshon, the son-in-law of the Timnite, because he took away his wife and gave her to his companion.” Then the Philistines went up and burned <dn>את</dn> her and <dn>את</dn> her father with fire. [7] And Shimshon said to them, “Though you do this, yet <dn>I</dn> shall take revenge on you, and after that <dn>I</dn> cease.” [8] And he struck <dn>את</dn> them hip and thigh, a great slaughter, and went down and dwelt in the cleft of the rock of Ěytam.

readings.subsection: The Birth and Rise of Shimshon
readings.title: The Jawbone of a Donkey
readings.subtitle: Empowered by the Spirit, Shimshon slays a thousand Philistines.
readings.text: [Judges 15:9] The Philistines then went up and encamped in Yehuḏah, and spread out against Leḥi. [10] And the men of Yehuḏah said, “Why have you come up against us?” And they answered, “We have come up to bind Shimshon, to do to him as he has done to us.” [11] Then three thousand men of Yehuḏah went down to the cleft of the rock of Ěytam and said to Shimshon, “Do you not know that the Philistines are rulers over us? Why have you done this to us?” And he said to them, “As they did to me, so <dn>I</dn> did to them.” [12] And they said to him, “We have come down to bind you, to give you into the hand of the Philistines.” And Shimshon said to them, “Swear to me not to fall on me yourselves.” [13] And they spoke to him, saying, “No, but we are certainly going to bind you, and shall give you into their hand but certainly not kill you.” So they bound him with two new ropes and brought him up from the rock. [14] When he came to Leḥi, the Philistines came shouting to meet him. And the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came mightily upon him. And the ropes that were on his arms became like flax that is burned with fire, and his bonds broke loose from his hands. [15] And he found a fresh jawbone of a donkey, and put out his hand and took it, and struck <dn>את</dn> a thousand men with it. [16] And Shimshon said, “With the jawbone of a donkey, one heap, two heaps, with the jawbone of a donkey <dn>I</dn> have stricken a thousand men!” [17] And it came to be, when he had ended speaking, that he threw <dn>את</dn> the jawbone from his hand, and called that place Ramath Leḥi. [18] And he became very thirsty, and cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and said, “<dn>You</dn> have given <dn>את</dn> this great deliverance by the hand of <dn>Your</dn> servant. And now, am <dn>I</dn> to die of thirst and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised?” [19] And <dn>Elohim</dn> split <dn>את</dn> the hollow place that is in Leḥi, and water came out, and he drank. And his spirit came back, and he revived. So he called its name Ěn Haqqore, which is in Leḥi to this day. [20] And he ruled Yisra’ěl twenty years in the days of the Philistines.
